notes: POC focused on sustained throughput guarantees and SLA crediting model. CTO (M. Alvarez) quote: "can't have tail >120ms p95 for 128-token responses". Primary ask: guaranteed baseline of 8,000 tokens/sec sustained across reserved pool (30-day rolling), with concurrency cap enforcement at 80 concurrent streams per pool. Burst policy requested: 2x baseline for up to 10 minutes per incident, with soft-prioritization rules (latency-first for priority routes). Want explicit credit formula if min tokens/sec not met: (shortfall_seconds * shortfall_tokens) -> token-credit % against monthly invoice; Redwood to provide monthly throughput report and token-level accounting. Prefers model families: quantized Llama-3-70B or Mistral-class 7B quantized at 8-bit; willing to accept 2-3% quality delta for 2x cost savings. Routing: primary region US-East, fallback to US-West with warm cache replication. Must support KV-prefix caching and automatic batching; prefer per-route concurrency limits. Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay premium for hard throughput SLA but want predictable unit economics (sustained vs burst pricing). Security: SSO (SAML), audit logs forwarded to SIEM, KMS integration for keys, EU residency for subset of data. Notes from call: AE ran through dedicated offering; SE demoed perf run (see perf notes). Legal returned SLA redlines 2026-03-09 (drive link). Next: finalize min tokens/sec language and concurrency enforcement in SLA, agree burst billing model, finalize hardware mapping (A100 vs H100), confirm EU region capacity availability.
